chunks.text: In November 2026, Anthropic, the U.S. company that makes the [[AI assistant]] Claude, held the largest [[initial public offering]] ever, by money raised. An initial public offering is a company's first sale of shares to the public. A share is a small piece of a company. Investors, people who buy shares to make money, {{snapped up}} the shares. Researchers who had {{broken away}} from OpenAI, the [[maker]] of ChatGPT, started Anthropic in 2021.

verbs.correct: To buy something quickly and eagerly
verbs.wrong: To give something a new name
verbs.why: Shoppers snap up cheap TVs on the first day of a sale. Fans snap up concert tickets in just a few minutes. Investors, people who buy shares to make money, snapped up the shares.

verbs.correct: To leave a group and start your own
verbs.wrong: To work hard for many long hours
verbs.why: Some players break away from a big club and start a new team. A few workers break away from their company and open their own shop. Researchers who had broken away from OpenAI started Anthropic in 2021.

chunks.text: On November 18, strong [[demand]] pushed the price to $83 a share, above the [[planned]] range of $70 to $78. The sale of 980 million shares {{brought in}} about $81 billion. That [[beat the record]] of $75 billion, set by the rocket company SpaceX in June 2026. Anthropic's seven [[founders]] {{cashed in}} about 24 million of their shares. Anthropic also {{lined up}} seven [[partners]], including Google and the chip maker Nvidia, to buy $26 billion more of its shares.

verbs.correct: To earn an amount of money
verbs.wrong: To borrow money from a bank
verbs.why: Her small shop brings in about $2,000 a month. The school fair brings in money for new books. The sale of 980 million shares brought in about $81 billion.

verbs.wrong: To hide something in a drawer
verbs.why: Many people cash in their savings bonds when they need money. My uncle cashes in his old baseball cards when his car needs repairs. Anthropic's seven founders cashed in about 24 million of their shares.

verbs.correct: To arrange for people to do something
verbs.wrong: To argue with someone about a price
verbs.why: She lines up a babysitter for every Saturday night. The coach lines up two new players before each season. Anthropic lined up seven partners, including Google and Nvidia, to buy $26 billion more of its shares.

chunks.text: [[Trading]] began on November 19 on the Nasdaq, a U.S. [[stock market]] where people buy and sell shares. The price {{shot up}} right away, to more than $111. But the shares did not {{hold on to}} those [[early gains]]. The price {{came down}} in the afternoon and {{ended up}} at about $97, about 17 percent above the sale price. Anthropic's [[market value]], the total value of all its shares, was then about $1.3 trillion, the British newspaper the Guardian reported.

verbs.wrong: To stop for a short time
verbs.why: Gas prices sometimes shoot up in the summer. His temperature shoots up at night when he is sick. On November 19, Anthropic's share price shot up right away, to more than $111.

verbs.wrong: To borrow something for a day
verbs.why: Good teams hold on to a lead until the end of the game. Some families hold on to their old homes for many years. Anthropic's shares did not hold on to their early gains on the first day.
The price of TVs comes down every year. My fever comes down after I take medicine. Anthropic's share price came down in the afternoon of its first day.

verbs.correct: To finally reach a certain level
verbs.wrong: To be sold to a single buyer
verbs.why: Our team often ends up in third place. Prices at the market sometimes end up higher than people expect. Anthropic's share price ended up at about $97, about 17 percent above the sale price.

chunks.text: In a report for investors, Anthropic listed [[risks]], such as people losing control of AI. Its [[chief executive]] said the company would take as long as needed to make its AI safe. On November 20, falling [[tech stocks]] helped {{drag Anthropic's shares down}}, a U.S. news channel reported. In November 2026, reports said OpenAI, Anthropic's main [[rival]], was {{holding off}} on its share sale until at least 2027.

verbs.correct: To pull something to a lower level
verbs.wrong: To last much longer than needed
verbs.why: Bad weather drags down sales at the beach shops. One weak player drags the whole team down. On November 20, falling tech stocks helped drag Anthropic's shares down.

Many families hold off on buying a new car when money is tight. She holds off on calling the doctor until she knows more. In November 2026, reports said OpenAI was holding off on its share sale until at least 2027.

mainIdea.s: Anthropic, the maker of Claude, raised more money in its first public sale of shares than any company before it. Its price rose fast on the first trading day, then fell from that high.
mainIdea.why: The sale brought in about $81 billion, a record. The price shot up at first, then came down and ended up at about $97.

mainIdea.s: Shares of the company that makes Claude climbed all day after they began trading on the Nasdaq. When the market closed, each one was worth well over $111, far more than early buyers paid.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the shares did not hold on to their early gains. The price came down in the afternoon and ended up at about $97.

mainIdea.s: An AI firm has decided to wait until next year to put its shares on sale. Its leaders say markets are too weak right now, and they want extra time to test their new safety tools first.
mainIdea.why: Anthropic did sell its shares in November 2026. Investors snapped them up, and the sale beat the record set by SpaceX.

lines.text: Did you follow the Anthropic news?
The company that makes Claude? I heard it started selling shares to the public.
Right. Investors {{snapped them up}}. The sale {{brought in}} about 81 billion dollars.
By money raised, yes. It beat the 75 billion SpaceX raised in June.
Anthropic sure knows how to [[make a splash]].
The price {{shot up}} [[right out of the gate]], to more than 111 dollars a share.
From 83? Did the shares {{hold on to}} that?
No. The price {{came down}} in the afternoon and {{ended up}} at about 97.
That's still way above 83. What [[a wild ride]] for one day.
And the next day, falling tech stocks {{dragged its shares down}}.
Did the people who started the company sell any shares?
The seven founders {{cashed in}} about 24 million of them. And the company {{lined up}} partners like Google and Nvidia to buy more.
Anthropic is in [[the big leagues]] now. Is OpenAI next?
Not yet. Reports said OpenAI was {{holding off}} on its own share sale until at least 2027.
Funny, since Anthropic's founders once {{broke away}} from OpenAI.
